title: Drive an allen bolt home with an L-key (Franka, operational-space control)
text:
1 small steel platform standing fixed on a sturdy table, each with an M16 threaded hole through its plate, and beside it: 1 L-shaped allen key lying on the table — the hole's M16 allen (socket-head) bolt already stands in it hand-started, a couple of turns captured. The hole carries real threads; the bolt head carries a 14 mm hex socket.
Goal: seat the key in the bolt's socket and drive it down (turn clockwise while pressing) until it seats. A seated bolt locks in place. The task is complete once the bolt is seated. The key holds in a firm pinch: close the fingers across either arm's hex and the grip locks; open wide to release.
success: Success, exactly: at the end of the run, the M16 allen bolt standing in the small steel platform's threaded hole has its threaded tip at least 22 mm below the top face of the platform's plate (it starts hand-started with the tip 4.898 mm below that face; the head bottoms out at 24.8 mm), the tip lies within 4 mm horizontally of the hole's vertical axis, and the bolt's axis, tip to head, is within 5° of the hole axis (head up). The depth part does not hold at the start; the position and tilt parts do. Nothing is required of the key or the gripper, and there is no speed condition. [scene.success() = every bolt seated(); bolt origin = its thread tip; plate top 0.038 m above the platform origin on the table top; platform at world (0.42, 0, 0)]
